The earliest outside verdicts on a successor were printed in its founders' own announcement (LibreOffice, Valkey) or were a foundation's taking it in (OpenTofu, Valkey, Forgejo). A response by an organization independent of the founders was found in four contested cases, after 0 to 1,189 days; three of the four were the speaker's announcement of its own move, and the one statement made before a move (Fedora's proposal to replace Redis) gave the licence as its only reason. The only verdict found dated before the move it decided is the Hudson community's rename vote (214 to 14), whose voters were the movers. Recognition went to the successor in both cases where the creator or the body of core maintainers moved (Jenkins, Libera Chat), split where part of the core moved (MariaDB, Valkey), and no successor took the original's name except io.js, by reunion. Only Hudson's line stopped producing, 2,294 days or fewer after the vote; the other originals still release.
